column2: Rehoboam goes to Shechem where all Israel comes to make him king, preserving both occurrences of the location.
The people introduce their address to Rehoboam after the selected absence of verse 2; Jeroboam is not inserted as spokesman here.
Heavy collar and harsh servitude are distinguished in the request for relief, followed by promised service.
column3: Collar preserves kloios; a different agricultural yoke image is not silently substituted.

column2: The king orders departure and return after a three-day interval, and the people depart.
column3: The exact reckoning of until three days and the third-day return in verse 12 remains conventional narrative timing, not an asserted seventy-two-hour wait.

column2: Elders who served the living Solomon are asked for counsel about answering the people, preserving the former service qualification.
Becoming a servant this day, serving and speaking good words precede the promise of their lasting service; the reversal is retained.
Abandoning elder counsel precedes consulting the young men raised with and attending him, retaining both descriptions.
The double advice/answer question repeats the people's collar-relief request, without adding a response yet.
The repeated instruction thus speak, reported complaint and little-part versus father's-loins boast remain.
column3: Little part interprets mikrotes minimally; finger or a particular sexual referent is not supplied as a settled reading.

column2: Added collar burden and the whip/scorpion contrast preserve the threat and future discipline language.
column3: Scorpions retains the image without deciding whether it names an implement or literal animals.

column2: All Israel returns on the third day according to the repeated royal instruction; Jeroboam is not added to the subject.
Harsh answer and renewed rejection of the elders' advice remain as separate narrative assertions.
The delivered answer repeats collar increase and whip/scorpion discipline but does not import the earlier little-part boast into this unit.
Failure to listen is explained by the Lord's turn of events establishing the Ahijah word concerning Jeroboam; divine causation remains explicit.
No Davidic share, no inheritance in Jesse's son, flight to tents and shepherd your house retain the complete revolt speech and subsequent departure.
Adoniram's tribute office, all-Israel stoning and death and Rehoboam's managed ascent and flight remain.
column3: No chariot is supplied in this account's unexpressed ascent object, unlike the explicit chariot in 24u.

column2: Israel's rejection of David's house lasts to the narrator's this day, without a modern historical endpoint.
Jeroboam's return from Egypt, summons, assembly and kingship precede the exception of Judah's scepter and Benjamin alone.
Judah and Benjamin muster one hundred twenty thousand young warriors to recover Rehoboam's kingdom; 180,000 is not substituted.
The Lord's word comes to Shemaiah identified as man of God, opening the command.
Rehoboam's parentage and Judah kingship, all Judah's house, Benjamin and the remaining people are separately addressed.
The double prohibition of ascent and fighting brothers, return-home command and divine origin of the matter lead to obedience and halted departure.
The alternate account repeats Solomon's death and burial, then gives Rehoboam age sixteen, twelve-year reign and Naanan daughter of Anan son of Nahash of Ammon.
column3: All selected ages, genealogy and evil/not-Davidic-way assessment remain without harmonization to the later royal summary.

column2: Jeroboam's Ephraim origin, mother Sarira a prostitute, staff-rule over Joseph's burdens, Sarira building, three hundred chariots, citadel and David-city work and royal uprising remain.
column3: Ruler of the staff is provisional; the repeated this-one builder here is retained as Jeroboam, without resolving the unnamed builder in 11:27. The possessive of the chariot clause remains open.

column2: Solomon seeks his death; the fearful Jeroboam escapes to Shishak and stays until Solomon dies, retaining the full repeated exile notice.
Jeroboam hears of the death, asks in Shishak's ears for release and receives an offer to request a gift; ordinary human address remains.
Ano, older sister of Thekemina, her prominence among royal daughters and birth of Abijah remain in this distinct marriage account.
column3: The appositional relationships and royal-daughter designation are preserved, not merged with Ader's similar marriage story.

column2: Emphatic release request, Egypt departure, Sarira arrival, all Ephraim's gathering and stockade construction remain.
The very severe illness, Jeroboam's going to inquire and instruction to Ano to ask God about survival remain.
column3: Jeroboam's own going is not removed to reconcile his subsequent sending of his wife.

column2: Ahijah at Shiloh is sixty and has the Lord's word; bread, little cakes for his children, grapes and a honey jar are specified.
column3: The pronoun his in for his children is retained without asserting whether Ahijah's or another household is intended.

column2: The woman's actual supplies include two cakes, and Ahijah's old age and dim eyesight remain.
column3: Two is retained only where stated here; the earlier general cake instruction is not retroactively numbered.

column2: The Sarira departure, city arrival and Ahijah's attendant sent to named Ano preserve the messenger scene and harsh divine announcement.
column3: No disguise or door-hearing detail from another account is inserted; skipped letter j remains absent.

column2: The why-question lists all gifts; behold introduces her departure, Sarira gate, her young women and their report of the child's death.
Behold, destruction of Jeroboam's wall-urinating males, dogs in the city, birds in the field and the child's lament with good word about the Lord remain.
column3: House and every male express the household-scoped idiom, not additional victims. Alas, lord is human lament; good word is not replaced with a broader moral verdict.

column2: The woman leaves upon hearing; at Sarira entry the child dies and the outcry meets her, preserving timing and auditory image.
Shechem assembly, Rehoboam arrival and Shemaiah the Elamite's unwashed new garment, twelve torn pieces, ten for clothing and final ten-tribes saying remain.
column3: The different prophet and setting are not harmonized to Ahijah's earlier scene; the final abbreviated oracle is not expanded with missing promises.

column2: The repeated complaint adds the burden of royal table food; the conditional relief/service and three-more-days reply remain distinctive.
Elders are summoned, the third-day answer discussed and the people's message repeated; their brief so-the-people-have-spoken response remains.
column3: The longer servant-counsel advice from verse 7 is not inserted into this shorter alternate exchange.

column2: Rejected advice, summoned companions, repeated complaint and little-part boast precede the different final verb rule with scorpions.
column3: Rule is not normalized to discipline from verse 11; little part remains unresolved rather than supplied finger.

column2: The saying pleases Rehoboam and determines his answer, with companions explicitly identified as young men.
All as one, each to his neighbor and the collective cry retain unity, no Davidic share, no Jesse inheritance and neither ruler nor leader judgment.
column3: Fit supplies an English predicate for the elliptical not-for-ruler clause; the translation does not add a new office or qualification test.

column2: Dispersal from Shechem, each tent, Rehoboam's departure and explicit chariot ascent, Jerusalem entry and both full scepters following remain.
column3: Took hold of himself is a provisional reflexive interpretation of objectless katekratesen; prevailing or retaining control remains a live alternative, not a settled emotional description.

column2: The beginning-year timing, every man of Judah and Benjamin, and attack toward Jeroboam at Shechem remain after the skipped v/w labels.
The repeated Shemaiah word retains all addressees, double prohibition, brothers identity, each return home and divine origin of the matter.
Hearing and refraining from going according to the Lord's word complete the alternate account without collapsing it into verse 24.
Jeroboam builds and inhabits Shechem, then leaves and builds Penuel, retaining sequence and both places.
Behold now and future return to David's house remain Jeroboam's inward assessment, not a narrator's prediction of actual return.
The conditional Jerusalem sacrifice, return of hearts to the Lord and their lord Rehoboam, and feared killing retain the two lord references.
column3: Capitalization interprets the first Lord as divine and second as royal; the coordination remains explicitly open rather than deleting one as repetition.

column2: Counsel, going and making two golden heifers retain the female designation; enough-going-to-Jerusalem and behold your gods preserve the king's claim.
column3: The narrator does not endorse the exodus claim; calves or bulls are not substituted for the selected heifers.

column2: One heifer is placed in Bethel and one in Dan, retaining both locations without additional shrines.
The matter becomes sin and the people go before the one as far as Dan, preserving the selected singular.
column3: The relation of before the one to the endpoint remains unresolved; movement to both images is not inserted.

column2: High-place houses and priests from a portion of the people who were not Levi's sons remain, without calling them the lowest class.
Eighth month, fifteenth day, analogy to Judah's feast, Bethel altar, sacrifice to made heifers and stationed high-place priests retain each ritual detail.
The date repeats, the feast is fashioned from his heart, and the repeated altar ascents culminate in sacrifice.
column3: The source's invented feast is not turned into an invented month clause; epithyo is retained as sacrifice without specifying incense alone.
